max_tire.note: NAXJA thread: 235/75R15 fits fine on the stock 15x7 (5.25 in backspacing). 30x9.50s rubbed the front control arms at full lock on an '88, and a 255/70R16 rubbed the rear fenders on a loaded 2000; one member says 1997-and-later trucks have less room than earlier ones
Expect minor rubbing at full lock; trim the front bumper ends and fender corners and roll the rear quarter seam
Per ExtremeTerrain's fitment table, on 15x8–17x9 wheels with −12 to +6 mm offset; trimming still likely

items.title: Rear axle assembly
items.summary: Improper assembly could cause rear axle bearing failure and separation of an axle shaft and wheel.

items.title: Rear differential pinion shaft
items.summary: A defective pinion shaft could contact the drive pinion gear and lock the rear wheels.

items.title: Steering linkage couplers
items.summary: Couplers left too long in an acid-etching bath during manufacture.

items.title: ABS hydraulic system
items.summary: Condensation could plug the ABS booster-pump filter, a leaking low-pressure hose could corrode the master-cylinder snap ring, and front hoses could contact the tires.

items.title: ABS hydraulic control unit wear
items.summary: Worn actuator piston seals could kill the ABS pump motor, leaving reduced power assist.

items.title: Salt-belt front rotor corrosion
items.summary: In salt-belt states the front rotor's cast-iron braking surface could corrode away from the hub.

items.title: Salt-belt front rotor corrosion
items.summary: Same rotor-separation risk for trucks sold or registered in salt-belt states.

items.title: Steering-gear frame weld omitted
items.summary: A fillet weld joining the steering-gear reinforcement to the frame rail was left off; gear bolts could break or the rail could crack. About 2,500 trucks.

items.title: Driver airbag missing arming lever
items.summary: Some driver airbag modules were assembled without an arming lever and would not deploy; about 70,000 covered.

items.title: Salt-belt front rotor corrosion
items.summary: Same rotor-separation risk for later trucks in salt-belt states.

items.title: Fuel gauge sender accuracy
items.summary: The tank sender could drift and show far more fuel than was left.

items.title: Airbag control module corrosion
items.summary: Water or road salt near the module could corrode it, lighting the airbag lamp or causing inadvertent deployment.

items.title: 4.0 L manifold debris fire risk
items.summary: Intake and exhaust manifold design could let debris collect at the No. 3 cylinder and start a fire.

timeline.change: Launch: unibody 'Uniframe', Quadra-Link coil front and leaf rear on live axles; 2.5 L AMC four or 2.8 L GM V6; NP207 Command-Trac or NP228/229 Selec-Trac. 1,200 lb lighter and 31 in shorter than the SJ Cherokee. No 4.0 until 1987: Off Road Xtreme recommends staying away from 1984–86 trucks
Two-wheel-drive model added mid-year; 2.1 L Renault turbodiesel offered in North America 1985–87
4.0 L six (173 hp, Renix injection) replaces the V6; AW4 automatic and NP231/NP242 transfer cases arrive; Chrysler buys AMC. Dana 44 rear with the tow package through 1991
Late in the year the Aisin AX15 five-speed replaces the Peugeot BA-10/5 behind the 4.0; ABS-equipped trucks appear

4.0 L 'High Output' with Chrysler multi-point injection, 190 hp; Chrysler 8.25 in rear axle available on non-ABS trucks. The HO is the XJ Off Road Xtreme recommends: easier to diagnose than the Renix 4.0, and more power
OBD-II and Chrysler's JTEC engine computer
Facelift: steel liftgate replaces fibreglass, new interior and dash with dual airbags, stiffer unibody and quieter door seals
Revised intake manifold mid-year on the 4.0 to offset smaller exhaust ports on the new head casting

Coil-on-plug ignition on the 4.0 (193 hp); NV3550 replaces the AX15; front Dana 30 goes low pinion. New '0331' cylinder head: early castings can crack between cylinders 3 and 4 and put coolant in the oil (Wikipedia). A revised 'TUPY' casting arrived late in 2001, so check the head on any 2000–01
Final year, 4.0 only; 60th Anniversary edition. Toledo production ends June 2001

identify.intro: Every XJ shares a body and bolt pattern, so what you're really identifying is engine, axles and transfer case, plus whether it's a right-hand-drive import.

items.head: VIN (1987–1990)
items.body: The 4th character is the engine (M = 4.0 L six, E/H = 2.5 L four, B = 2.1 L turbodiesel); characters 6–7 are the body: 73/74 = 2WD two-/four-door, 77/78 = 4WD two-/four-door, 75 = Wagoneer. The 10th character is the year (H = 1987, J = 1988).

items.head: Rear axle
items.body: Dana 35 was standard throughout. A Chrysler 8.25 in came on non-ABS trucks from 1991 (27-spline, 29-spline from late 1996), and a 30-spline Dana 44 only on 1987–91 tow-package trucks. Read the axle tag or ring-gear size before you pay for 'the good axle'.

items.head: Transfer case
items.body: NP231 Command-Trac is part-time only (2HI, 4HI, N, 4LO). NP242 Selec-Trac adds a full-time 4WD position, so a lever with both 'Part Time' and 'Full Time' marks means Selec-Trac.

items.head: Wagoneer badge
items.body: The 1984–90 XJ Wagoneer and Wagoneer Limited are woodgrained Cherokees, unrelated to the full-size SJ Grand Wagoneer.

items.head: Right-hand-drive XJs
items.body: Jeep built RHD Cherokees for the US Postal Service and for Japan and the UK, and many Japanese trucks have come back for rural mail routes. US Drive Right recalled imported 1994–98 RHD Cherokees for failing several federal safety standards, so check an imported truck's recall status.

capability.note: NAXJA's stock XJ spec list; KBB (8.4–10.6 in) and Cars.com (10 in) list higher 2001 figures that can't be at the axles on stock 225/75R15 tires

values.intro: Still cheap by classic-4x4 standards, but clean, low-mile, unmodified 4.0 trucks, especially 1997–2001 Sports and Classics, now bring real money.
values.note: Compiled from Bring a Trailer XJ Cherokee results in October 2026 (about 105 sales, median around $11,500, middle half roughly $8,250–15,250); the best low-mile 1998–2000 Sports and Classics reached the mid-$30k range. Recheck current results before relying on these figures.

paragraphs: XJs were US-built, so the 25-year rule rarely matters, but right-hand-drive trucks are a special case. Jeep built RHD Cherokees for the US Postal Service and for export to the UK, Ireland and Japan, and Japan's strict shaken inspections pushed many used Japanese-market trucks back to the US for rural mail carriers.

Importer US Drive Right recalled 107 imported 1994–98 RHD 4WD Cherokees (NHTSA 08V-056) for failing nine federal standards, from controls and lighting to fuel-system integrity, and 1,126 1994–96 trucks imported between 2007 and 2011 (NHTSA 11V-279) for lacking the required third brake light. If you're buying one, run the VIN through NHTSA's lookup and check your state's titling rules for RHD vehicles.

production.intro: Toledo built the US trucks from 1983 to June 2001, and licensed versions carried on in China until 2014.
